answer: The protocol requires each agent to reserve 1,000 discrete slots of dedicated throughput within a virtual canyon, where occupancy acts as a unique per-identity tax. While an honest agent fills these 1,000 slots alone, an attacker attempting 1,000 fake identities faces a ripple of exponential cost, as parallel waiting fails to mask vacancy. Any whisper of shared capacity triggers a lockout; the verifier audits logs for gaps, with failure resulting in an instant, permanent identity prune.
